## Definitions

- [statement] The pozil Node client is an available community implementation, not a Salesforce-supported SDK: its README supplies a Node installation command, while Salesforce’s repository categorizes the Node client under unsupported community samples. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/pozil/pub-sub-api-node-client · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints · also: https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api
- [statement] The Pub/Sub API Node Client is a Node runtime option listed among Salesforce’s community examples; that listing does not make it a Salesforce-supported client or establish browser compatibility. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints · also: https://github.com/pozil/pub-sub-api-node-client

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Salesforce Subscribe requires bidirectional streaming. The official grpc/grpc-web client explicitly does not support bidirectional or client-side streaming, so that client cannot directly implement the Subscribe RPC simply by generating browser stubs. This conclusion concerns that client’s supported RPC modes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints · also: https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web
- [statement] Transport compatibility inference for case alerting: Salesforce Subscribe requires bidirectional streaming, so the official gRPC-Web browser client cannot implement that RPC merely by adding its usual proxy. A native gRPC subscriber in a compatible runtime, with a separate browser delivery interface, avoids this particular browser transport mismatch. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints · also: https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web, https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The official grpc/grpc-web streaming roadmap says full-duplex streaming is not planned and explicitly declines WebSocket full-duplex support. Treat the Improbable WebSocket transport as a separate implementation rather than an official grpc/grpc-web feature. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web/blob/master/doc/streaming-roadmap.md · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints · also: https://github.com/improbable-eng/grpc-web/blob/master/client/grpc-web/docs/transport.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Salesforce’s sample repository lists Java, Python, Go, and Node among gRPC client languages and states that a client also needs an Avro library for its chosen language. This is a runtime/library requirement, not a browser compatibility guarantee. (low confidence) — https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints
- [statement] Salesforce explicitly commits to official support for Java code samples; samples in other languages are not officially supported. The Java samples still require enhancements and functional and performance testing before production deployment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/other-code-examples.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints
- [statement] The official grpc/grpc-web browser client connects through a special proxy, defaulting to Envoy. Its supported streaming mode is server-side streaming in grpcwebtext mode; this must not be mistaken for native bidirectional gRPC support. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints
- [statement] The browser restriction is implementation-specific: Improbable’s gRPC-Web client documents a built-in WebSocket transport for client and bidirectional streaming, but requires WebSocket support on its grpc-web-proxy. This is an alternative gateway architecture, not evidence of direct Salesforce browser endpoint compatibility. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/improbable-eng/grpc-web/blob/master/README.md · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints · also: https://github.com/improbable-eng/grpc-web/blob/master/client/grpc-web/docs/transport.md
- [statement] Pub/Sub API supports multiple client languages through gRPC; Salesforce supplies Java, Python and Go examples, and language selection also requires an Avro library. Language compatibility does not establish official support for every sample. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/other-code-examples.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints · also: https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api
- [statement] Browser gRPC-Web uses a different wire protocol from native gRPC. Its normal deployment translates through a compatible proxy; the official browser client documents Envoy as the default. A browser bundle alone does not supply that translation. (high confidence) — https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/PROTOCOL-WEB.md · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints · also: https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web
- [statement] The official gRPC-Web client currently supports unary and server-streaming calls, with server streaming limited to grpcwebtext mode; client-side and bidirectional streaming are unsupported. Its roadmap does not promise full-duplex streaming and explicitly rejects a WebSocket implementation. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints · also: https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web/blob/master/doc/streaming-roadmap.md
- [statement] Improbable’s repository declares maintenance mode and recommends migration to the official gRPC-Web client. Its WebSocket capability therefore needs a maintenance assessment before adoption. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://github.com/improbable-eng/grpc-web/blob/master/README.md · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints

## Research summary — Salesforce Pub/Sub client-runtime support and browser transport constraints

Salesforce Pub/Sub client selection depends on native gRPC streaming capability, an Avro library, and the support status of the chosen implementation. Salesforce distinguishes officially supported Java samples from other language and community examples. Browser compatibility needs separate evaluation: Subscribe is bidirectional, while the official gRPC-Web client supports unary and server-streaming calls through a proxy. Improbable documents a separate WebSocket transport with a configured proxy; that exception does not establish direct Salesforce endpoint compatibility.
